title: Event sourcing
description: Learn about event sourcing for persisting state as a sequence of events. Understand how to reconstruct state and benefit from audit trails.

data.text: Event sourcing persists state as a sequence of events rather than storing the current state. Instead of overwriting data, you record every change as an event. The current state is reconstructed by replaying these events.
In traditional CRUD, you store the current state. In event sourcing, you store the history of state changes.

items: Store state-changing events instead of current state
Events are immutable—never modified or deleted
Current state is reconstructed by replaying events
Provides complete audit trail of all changes
Enables temporal queries—state at any point in time

data.title: Key Benefit
data.text: Event sourcing provides a complete audit trail and enables you to understand how the system reached its current state. This is invaluable for debugging and compliance.

items: Command: Request to change state
Event: Record of the state change
Event Store: Append-only log of events
Projection: Read model built from events
Replay: Reconstruct state by replaying events

items.title: CRUD
items.description: Store current state. Simple to understand. No audit trail. Hard to reconstruct past state. Overwrites history.

items.title: Event Sourcing
items.description: Store event history. Complete audit trail. Can reconstruct any past state. More complex. Events are immutable.

items: Complete audit trail of all changes
Debug by replaying events to understand what happened
Temporal queries—state at any point in time
Natural fit for event-driven architectures
Events can be published to other systems
Parallel read models via projections
More complex mental model
Event schema evolution is challenging
Replaying events can be slow for long histories
Requires different query patterns
Event store can grow very large
Learning curve for the team

data.title: Not for Everything
data.text: Event sourcing adds significant complexity. Use it selectively for domains where the audit trail and replay capabilities provide real value.

items: When audit trails are critical (financial, legal)
When you need to understand how state evolved
When temporal queries are required
When building event-driven architectures
When complex business logic benefits from event history
Design events to be immutable and facts
Use snapshots for performance with long event histories
Version your event schemas carefully
Implement event schema migration strategies
Use CQRS with event sourcing for read optimization
Monitor event store size and performance
